premises.text: Mobile app development requires many languages and frameworks, so it is expensive and slow even for simple apps
premises.evidence_span: mobile application development is hard. It requires knowledge of many programming languages, technologies, and frameworks. And because of that, it's expensive

premises.text: A PowerPoint-like drag-and-drop editor with a flexible component library lets non-technical users build customizable apps
premises.evidence_span: a non-technical user can drag and drop components and build their own awesome mobile app

premises.text: Apps built on the platform are native for look, feel, and performance
premises.evidence_span: the apps that are built are native. And the reason that's important to the user, it gives them the best look, feel, and performance

premises.text: A preview app lets builders test and interact with the application live on a mobile device while building
premises.evidence_span: We also have a preview app. This allows you to test and interact with the application as you're building it live on your mobile device

value.text: Non-technical users can build real mobile apps as easily as PowerPoint
value.evidence_span: building mobile apps was as easy as PowerPoint

causal_links.evidence_span: An average app takes $27,000 to create
If you can build a PowerPoint slide deck, you too can become a mobile app developer

notes: Demo feature list (map, RSS, gallery, social buttons) folded into drag-drop component-library mechanism (§4.1.7). Native output and live preview split because speaker highlights them as distinct product conditions. Future WordPress/marketplace roadmap treated as vision framing and omitted (§4.1.4). Market-size framing excluded. Two-domain partition.
